We do not use automated evaluation metrics and instead use human evaluations for two reasons. First, there are currently no metrics in the literature that assess whether the returned reasoning chains are "correct" from a commonsense perspective. Second, evaluating dialog systems is challenging.

Participants interacted with the system, answered generated questions, validated returned reasoning chains, and provided novel knowledge when proofs were missing.

Users were asked to validate whether the reasoning chains are "correct" from a commonsense perspective and to provide explanations if they rejected the proofs. The dialog system presented multiple-choice options and collected open-domain text explanations formatted as if-then statements.
